terms.grammar: pronoun, first person plural: dative and ablative nōbīs
evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.14.1: sī vōs valētis, nōs valēmus
terms.comment: Left out unless stressed (sī vōs valētis, nōs valēmus). Of the genitives, nostrum is “of us” as part of the group (nēmō nostrum, none of us; utrīusque nostrum, of each of us), nostrī the object of a feeling (nostrī amantius). “With us” is nōbīscum. Writers of letters often say “we” of themselves: haec properantēs scrīpsimus, I wrote this in a hurry.

phrases.english: If you are well, we are well.
Let’s go; lead us there, please.

phrases.latin: nēmō nostrum nōn peccat. hominēs sumus, nōn deī
phrases.english: None of us doesn’t do wrong. We are human, not gods.
The houses of both of us are going up apace.

phrases.latin: advolā ad nōs eō animō ut nōs amēs, tē amārī sciās. cētera cōram agēmus. haec properantēs scrīpsimus.
phrases.english: Fly to us, in the spirit of loving us and knowing you are loved. The rest we’ll settle face to face. I wrote this in a hurry.
